title: Quantitative determination of perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in soil, water, and home garden produce
author: Huset, M. Barry
materials: All prepared samples or extracts were analyzed using an Agilent 1100 HPLC (Santa Clara, California) and a Waters Quattro Micro tandem mass spectrometer (Milford, Massachusetts). Aliquots of prepared samples or extracts were injected onto the HPLC system and separated via reversed phase chromatography. HPLC conditions and gradients used are found in Table 1, Table 2, Table 3. The tandem mass spectrometer was operated in ESI- mode, with multiple reaction monitoring windows used to maximize sensitivity. Tandem mass spectrometer (MS/MS) conditions are found in Table 4, Table 5. Multiple transitions, when available, were monitored for each analyte and multiple reaction monitoring (MRM) was used to maximize signal for each analyte. steps.title: Prepare water samples
steps.instruction: Transfer 150 μL of each water sample into a 2 mL polypropylene autosampler vial, add 50 μL of internal‑standard stock solution (3 ng/mL in acetonitrile), mix briefly, and keep ready for analysis.

steps.title: Prepare soil samples
steps.instruction: Air‑dry soil, sieve through a #16 stainless‑steel sieve (retain a portion for wet‑weight determination). For each 5 g soil aliquot, add 50 μL of internal‑standard stock (100 ng/mL). Extract by three successive rounds of sonication and shaking with 7 mL methanol containing 1 % ammonium hydroxide per round. Collect and combine supernatants, evaporate to dryness under nitrogen, then reconstitute twice with 0.5 mL acetonitrile. Clean up the reconstituted extract with 25–40 mg graphitized carbon black, transfer 100 μL to an autosampler vial and dilute with 25 μL acetonitrile and 375 μL reagent water.

substeps.instruction: Air‑dry and sieve soil; retain a portion for wet‑weight determination.
Weigh 5 g of soil into a tube.
Spike with 50 μL of internal‑standard stock (100 ng/mL).
Add 7 mL methanol + 1 % NH₄OH; sonicate and shake.
Repeat extraction two more times with fresh 7 mL methanol + 1 % NH₄OH.
Combine all supernatants and evaporate to dryness under nitrogen.
Reconstitute with 0.5 mL acetonitrile, vortex, then add another 0.5 mL acetonitrile and vortex again.
Add 25–40 mg graphitized carbon black, mix, and allow cleanup.
Transfer 100 μL of the cleaned extract to an autosampler vial.
Dilute with 25 μL acetonitrile and 375 μL reagent water.

steps.title: Prepare produce samples
steps.instruction: Remove skins, stems, and seeds as appropriate, homogenize the edible portion, and weigh 5 g aliquots. Add 50 μL of internal‑standard stock (25 ng/mL). Add 2 g magnesium sulfate and three extraction rounds of 10 mL acetonitrile containing 1 % ammonium hydroxide. Combine supernatants, evaporate to dryness under nitrogen, reconstitute twice with 350 μL acetonitrile, clean up with 25–40 mg graphitized carbon black, transfer 70 μL to an autosampler vial and dilute with 55 μL acetonitrile and 375 μL reagent water.

substeps.instruction: Trim produce (remove skins, stems, seeds) and homogenize.
Weigh 5 g of homogenate into a tube.
Spike with 50 μL of internal‑standard stock (25 ng/mL).
Add 2 g magnesium sulfate.
Add 10 mL acetonitrile + 1 % NH₄OH; vortex and shake.
Repeat extraction two more times with fresh 10 mL acetonitrile + 1 % NH₄OH.
Combine all supernatants and evaporate to dryness under nitrogen.
Reconstitute with 350 μL acetonitrile, vortex, then add another 350 μL acetonitrile and vortex again.
Add 25–40 mg graphitized carbon black, mix for cleanup.
Transfer 70 μL of the cleaned extract to an autosampler vial.
Dilute with 55 μL acetonitrile and 375 μL reagent water.

steps.title: Configure HPLC‑MS/MS system
steps.instruction: Install a Thermo Betasil C8 analytical column (50 × 2.1 mm, 3 μm) with an Upchurch PEEK 0.5 μm pre‑filter and a Thermo Betasil C8 guard column (3.0 × 30 mm, 5 μm). Set column temperature to 30 °C and sample compartment to 5 °C. Use injection volumes of 10–20 μL. Prepare mobile phase A (0.1 % formic acid in water) and mobile phase B (0.1 % formic acid in acetonitrile). Program gradient elution as listed in Table 2 for PFPeA, PFHxA, PFOA, PFBS, PFHxS, PFOS and Table 3 for PFBA (see raw table strings below). Set flow rates as indicated in the tables. Connect the Agilent 1100 HPLC to a Waters Quattro Micro tandem mass spectrometer operated in negative‑ESI mode. Set source parameters (Table 4): capillary 0.40 kV, extractor 1 V, RF lens 0.2 V, source temperature 120 °C, desolvation temperature 350 °C, desolvation gas flow 700 L h⁻¹, cone gas flow 0 L h⁻¹. Set analyzer parameters (Table 5): LM1 resolution 10.0, HM1 resolution 10.0, ion energy 11.0 eV, entrance –5 V, collision 15 eV, exit 1 V; LM2 resolution 13.0, HM2 resolution 13.0, ion energy 21.5 eV, multiplier 750 V, gas‑cell Pirani pressure 3.0 × 10⁻³ mbar. Load MRM transitions exactly as listed in Table 6 (Q1 > Q3, retention time, dwell, cone, collision energy, delay).

substeps.instruction: Install analytical column (Thermo Betasil C8, 50 × 2.1 mm, 3 μm) with 0.5 μm pre‑filter and guard column (Thermo Betasil C8, 3.0 × 30 mm, 5 μm).
Set column temperature to 30 °C; set sample compartment to 5 °C.
Set injection volume to 10–20 μL.
Prepare mobile phase A (0.1 % formic acid in water) and mobile phase B (0.1 % formic acid in acetonitrile).

Program gradient for PFBA (Table 3):
"070300.42.070300.4"
Set flow rates as indicated in the tables.
Connect Agilent 1100 HPLC to Waters Quattro Micro MS/MS; select negative‑ESI mode.
Set source parameters (Table 4): capillary 0.40 kV, extractor 1 V, RF lens 0.2 V, source temperature 120 °C, desolvation temperature 350 °C, desolvation gas flow 700 L h⁻¹, cone gas flow 0 L h⁻¹.

Set analyzer parameters (Table 5): LM1 resolution 10.0, HM1 resolution 10.0, ion energy 11.0 eV, entrance –5 V, collision 15 eV, exit 1 V; LM2 resolution 13.0, HM2 resolution 13.0, ion energy 21.5 eV, multiplier 750 V, gas‑cell Pirani pressure 3.0 × 10⁻³ mbar.

steps.title: Run sample analysis
steps.instruction: Inject each prepared extract (using the injection volume specified above) onto the configured HPLC‑MS/MS system, acquire data in negative‑ESI MRM mode, and process the chromatograms according to the transitions listed in Table 6.
